text:
Asian maize/corn borer (Ostrinia furnacalis, also referenced together with Sesamia inferens in the pest glossary), rated as a high-importance pest.

Description: larvae are cream/whitish with dark spots along the body. Eggs are laid in clusters on the underside of leaves near the midrib; young larvae initially feed on leaves before boring into the stalk.

Damage: larvae tunnel into the stalk, weakening it and increasing the risk of lodging; they also bore into the ear shank and cob, causing direct kernel damage and yield loss, and creating entry points for secondary disease (such as stalk and ear rot).
